## Granada, One of Nicaragua's Oldest Cities

### Granada, Nicaragua's Colonial Jewel!

Granada is one of the country's most beautiful cities. Founded in 1524, it is regarded as the oldest city established by the Spanish on the isthmus between North and South America.

## Granada, Nicaragua's Cultural Capital!

The city has preserved many beautiful buildings from the colonial era. Highlights include La Casa de los Leones, the city's first Spanish church, Iglesia de San Francisco, and the “white fortress” of La Pólvora. There are also the inviting streets of the old town, where visitors can browse attractive souvenirs or sit down for coffee in one of the many small cafés. History lovers will also appreciate the Museum of Archaeology and History in Rivas, known as the “city of mangoes.”

Grey Glacier lies in Torres del Paine National Park in Chilean Patagonia. Its broad wall of ice reaches the lake, where broken-off ice floes drift on the water.

While navigating toward the glacier, visitors enjoy views of ice, water and mountain slopes. This boat trip complements the park's walking routes, lakes and steppe landscapes.

The glacier features on Torres del Paine itineraries alongside walks and stops at viewpoints. The exact order of the waterborne and walking sections is specified in the selected tour program.

Guachipas lies in the Lerma Valley south of Salta. On routes through northern Argentina, travelers pass through this small rural village with its low houses, main square and Church of the Immaculate Conception. Beyond the residential streets, hills and the valley open up, while local life remains closely connected to the land and regional traditions.

An interpretation center on the square introduces visitors to the area's rock art before a trip to Cuevas Pintadas near Las Juntas. Guachipas village and the archaeological site are two distinct places: in the village, visitors discover local culture, while the ancient paintings have survived in rock shelters beyond it.
